backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum coefficient linearly from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by updating the momentum value in the Muon param-group dict each step before the optimizer step. Leave all other Muon settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside the Muon update from 5 to 3. This makes each optimizer step cheaper so more steps fit in the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients and everything else as they are. Compare throughput and final val_bpb against baseline.
backlog.title: Muon Newton-Schulz steps 5 to 3

backlog.spec: Add a small decoupled weight decay (0.01 times the LR, AdamW style) to the Adam-optimized embedding and lm_head parameters, which currently receive none. Apply it inside the Adam step as p.mul_(1 - lr*wd) before the gradient update. Keep the scalar parameters without decay.
backlog.title: Decoupled weight decay on embeddings and lm_head

backlog.spec: Raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008 while leaving EMBEDDING_LR, MATRIX_LR and SCALAR_LR unchanged. This tests whether the output projection is under-trained in the short budget. Single-constant change only.
backlog.title: Higher lm_head learning rate

backlog.spec: Scale each Muon orthogonalized update by max(1, rows/cols)^0.5 so that tall matrices (MLP up-projection) get a proportionally larger step than wide ones. Apply this multiplier right before the parameter update inside the Muon step. Keep MATRIX_LR unchanged so only the relative scaling across matrix shapes changes.
backlog.title: Muon update shape scaling

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.95) for the Adam groups. This increases momentum smoothing on the noisy embedding and scalar gradients. Only the beta1 constant is modified.
backlog.title: Lower beta1 for Adam scalars and embeddings

backlog.spec: Multiply the Muon learning rate of transformer block i by a factor (0.85)^(DEPTH-1-i), so earlier layers get smaller updates than later layers and the deepest layer keeps MATRIX_LR. Implement by creating one Muon param group per layer with its own lr. Leave the schedule multiplier applied on top of each group's base lr.
backlog.title: Depth-decayed Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Increase WARMDOWN_RATIO from 0.5 to 0.7 so the learning rate decays over the final 70 percent of the time budget instead of 50 percent. Keep WARMUP_RATIO at 0 and FINAL_LR_FRAC at 0. Single-constant change.
backlog.title: Longer linear warmdown

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown multiplier with a cosine decay from 1 to FINAL_LR_FRAC over the warmdown window, computed as 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress)) where progress runs from 0 to 1 across the warmdown. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO unchanged.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps linearly from 0 over the first 2 percent of the time budget before the existing warmdown begins. This guards against early instability at the high embedding and scalar learning rates. Only the warmup constant changes, plus confirming the schedule function handles a nonzero warmup.
backlog.title: Short warmup before warmdown

backlog.spec: Replace the warmdown multiplier with 1 - sqrt(progress) over the warmdown window, where progress goes from 0 to 1 at the end of the time budget. This keeps the learning rate higher for longer than linear decay and drops sharply at the end. Apply to all groups and keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5.
backlog.title: Sqrt-shaped cooldown

backlog.spec: Tie the lm_head weight to the token embedding matrix so they share one parameter, removing the separate unembedding matrix. Use EMBEDDING_LR for the shared tensor and drop the UNEMBEDDING_LR group. Freed parameters can be reinvested by increasing DEPTH by one, keeping ASPECT_RATIO so model_dim stays consistent.
backlog.title: Tied embeddings and lm_head

backlog.spec: If the model applies a tanh logit softcap, change its cap value from its current setting to 30 (or from 30 to 15 if already 30; test the other direction only if the current cap is 15). Apply the cap as cap*tanh(logits/cap) before the cross-entropy loss. Single-constant change.
backlog.title: Logit softcap value

backlog.spec: Set the number of key/value heads to half the number of query heads (n_kv_head = n_head // 2), with each KV head shared by two query heads via repeat-interleave before attention. This reduces KV projection parameters and memory bandwidth. Keep model_dim and head count unchanged.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with fewer KV heads

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 100000 when precomputing the RoPE cos/sin tables. Longer base gives lower-frequency components better suited to the context length used here. Only the base constant changes.
backlog.title: RoPE base frequency

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSLL" so half of the layers in an 8-layer model use full context. This increases attention compute but may improve modeling of long-range dependencies. Only the pattern string changes.
backlog.title: Window pattern with more full-context layers

backlog.spec: Change DEPTH from 8 to 10 and ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 52 so model_dim stays near 512 while adding two layers. Keep HEAD_DIM unchanged and verify model_dim is divisible by HEAD_DIM after rounding. Adjust only these constants.
backlog.title: Deeper, narrower model

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from sequential residual updates (x = x + attn(norm(x)); x = x + mlp(norm(x))) to a parallel form x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)) using one shared pre-norm. This removes one sequential dependency per layer and can speed up each step. Keep the rest of the block unchanged.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks

backlog.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step covers half as many tokens and more steps occur within the 300 s budget. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE and the gradient accumulation logic consistent so the accumulation count is recomputed correctly. Single-constant change.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch for more steps

backlog.spec: Start with TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE at 2**17 and linearly grow it to 2**19 over the first 60 percent of the time budget, rounding each step's gradient accumulation count to an integer. This gives many cheap early updates and larger late batches for lower gradient noise. Recompute accumulation steps each iteration from the current batch target.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp

backlog.spec: Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 after the backward pass and before the optimizer step, using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_ over all trainable parameters. This prevents occasional spikes from destabilizing the high learning rates. Do not change any learning rate.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits, dim=-1)^2) to the cross-entropy loss to keep output logits from drifting in scale. Compute it on the same logits used for the main loss, in float32. Leave all other training code unchanged.
backlog.title: Logit z-loss regularization

backlog.spec: Train on shorter sequences early and grow to the full context length: use half the context length for the first 30 percent of the time budget, then the full length. Keep the number of tokens per optimizer step fixed by adjusting the batch size in sequences so TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE is unchanged. Recompile or reset attention masks at the switch point as needed.
backlog.title: Sequence length curriculum

backlog.spec: Maintain an EMA copy of model parameters with decay 0.999, updated after each optimizer step. Run the final evaluation with the EMA weights swapped in. Do not modify the evaluation call itself; only swap parameter values before the evaluation runs, and keep the live training weights unchanged.
backlog.title: Exponential moving average of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: During the last 20 percent of the time budget, accumulate a running uniform average of model parameters taken every 50 steps. Before final evaluation, copy the averaged weights into the model. This approximates checkpoint averaging and often smooths the end of a warmdown. Keep the training loop otherwise unchanged.
backlog.title: Weight averaging over final training window

backlog.spec: Enable fused=True on the Adam optimizer constructor and set torch.compile to use the default mode with dynamic=False so the graph is specialized once. This is a pure throughput change intended to raise steps within the fixed 300 s budget. Confirm the optimizer still receives the same parameter groups.
backlog.title: Fused Adam and torch.compile settings

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of each attention and MLP block to zero so every block starts as identity, and keep the other weights at their current init. This can make early training more stable when learning rates are high. Only the initialization of those output projections changes.
backlog.title: Zero-initialized residual output projections

backlog.spec: Add one learnable scalar per block that multiplies the attention and MLP branch outputs before they are added to the residual stream, initialized to 1.0 and trained with SCALAR_LR. This lets the model learn how much each layer contributes. Keep the number of added parameters negligible.
backlog.title: Per-layer learned residual scaling

backlog.spec: Confirm the MLP uses squared ReLU, relu(x)**2, between the up and down projections, and if it instead uses GELU switch to relu(x)**2 with the hidden width kept the same. Squared ReLU is often better per parameter at this scale. Only the activation function changes.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU MLP activation check

backlog.spec: Add one extra linear head (shape model_dim x vocab) that predicts the token two positions ahead, reusing the final hidden states. Training loss = CE(next token) + 0.1 * CE(token t+2), with the t+2 targets built by shifting the target tensor by one more position and masking the last position. Use only the next-token head at evaluation and do not change the evaluation call. The auxiliary head is trained with the Adam group used for lm_head.
backlog.title: Multi-token prediction auxiliary head

backlog.spec: In the attention blocks, make every odd-indexed layer reuse the key and value projections of the layer directly before it (c_k and c_v are not created for odd layers, so the layer only has its own query and output projections). Keep RoPE and QK-norm as they are. This cuts attention parameters by about a quarter, and the saved parameter budget can be spent on the same width, which should give more steps in 300 s.
backlog.title: Cross-layer KV sharing in attention pairs

backlog.spec: In CausalSelfAttention, apply RoPE only to the first half of each head's dimensions and leave the second half unrotated, so half of the query/key channels carry position-free content matching. Implement by slicing q and k before the rotary call and concatenating them back. No new parameters, and the sliding-window pattern and head count stay the same.
backlog.title: Partial NoPE: half the heads without rotary embedding

backlog.spec: Before the output projection c_proj, multiply each attention head's output by a learned sigmoid gate computed from the block input: gate = sigmoid(Linear(model_dim, n_head)(x)), initialised with bias 2.0 so gates start near 1. Apply it per head after the attention output is reshaped to (B, T, n_head, head_dim). Train the gate Linear with the Muon matrix group, since it is a 2D weight.
backlog.title: Per-head sigmoid output gating on attention

backlog.spec: Replace the single linear warmdown with a schedule that runs LR multiplier = 1 until 60% of the time budget, then drops to 0.3 and follows a cosine decay to 0.0 at 100%. This is a one-time warm restart in LR, not a warmup. Apply the same multiplier to all optimizer groups. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO logic and the time-based progress variable so the schedule stays wall-clock based.
backlog.title: Single cosine warm restart at 60% of budget

backlog.spec: During training only, for each transformer block except the first and last, skip the block's residual contribution with probability p_l, where p_l rises linearly with depth from 0 at layer 0 to 0.1 at the penultimate layer. When a block is skipped, pass its input through unchanged. Scale nothing at eval time, and disable dropping under torch.no_grad or in eval mode. This is stochastic depth with a fixed schedule and needs no tuning beyond the 0.1 cap.
backlog.title: Layer-drop regularization with depth-increasing rate

backlog.spec: Split the Muon matrix parameters into two groups: attention query and key weights get learning rate 0.5 * MATRIX_LR, while value, attention output, and MLP weights keep MATRIX_LR. Keep the same momentum, weight decay, and Newton-Schulz steps. Build the two param groups where the Muon groups are currently constructed, using the parameter names to route each matrix. This tests whether the attention logit matrices need a smaller step size.
backlog.title: Separate Muon learning rates for QK and value/output matrices

backlog.spec: Replace the Adam update for the token embedding weights with a Lion-style update: keep one momentum buffer m, update m = beta2*m + (1-beta2)*grad with beta2 = 0.99, and apply param -= lr * sign(beta1*m + (1-beta1)*grad) with beta1 = 0.9 and EMBEDDING_LR unchanged. Leave lm_head and scalars on Adam. Use a decoupled weight decay of 0 for this group. Reduces the optimizer-state footprint and tests whether sign-based steps suit the sparse embedding rows.
backlog.title: Lion-style sign update for the embedding table

backlog.spec: Build a per-position segment id by incrementing a counter at each beginning-of-document token that the existing data loader already produces (use the loader's own BOS marker, with no reference to prepare.py internals). Mask attention so each query can only attend to keys with the same segment id, combined with the existing causal and sliding-window masks. Keep the flash-attention path if it accepts a mask, or fall back to a boolean mask otherwise. This stops context leaking across unrelated documents in the packed sequences.
backlog.title: Document-boundary attention reset

backlog.spec: Apply dropout with rate 0.05 to the token embedding output (after the initial norm, before the first block), with the mask resampled per token and per training step. Use inverted scaling (divide by 0.95) during training and skip it entirely at evaluation. This is the only regularizer on the input path, and the existing weight decay and z-loss settings are left untouched. Set the rate through a single module-level constant so it can be toggled to 0.
backlog.title: Input embedding dropout

memo:
Incumbent is mean_adjusted 1.0987 (slot 11, official 1.0987), set by cutting TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2^19 to 2^18 (-0.0158). More optimizer steps in the fixed 300 s is the one clear win. Batch/step-count changes helped most.

Small gains that were rejected: momentum ramp (-0.0020), embedding/lm_head weight decay (-0.0019), gradient clipping (-0.0093 delta, two runs at 1.0906/1.0883), sequence curriculum (-0.0082, two runs at 1.0918/1.0893). Several of these are probably real but were judged against the earlier incumbent. Re-test them on top of 2^18.

Hurt: branch scales (+0.0042), weight averaging (+0.0037), t+2 head (+0.0049), warmup 0.02 (+0.0123). Drop these.

Next: try gradient clipping and the momentum ramp on the new baseline, then combine them. Try an even smaller batch, such as 2^17. Use short single-line SEARCH text to avoid patch failures. Avoid the logsumexp regularizer, which was flagged for target_leak.
